title: Unified record envelope (v1)
description: The canonical, backend-agnostic wire form of ANY think-and-ship record — a think step, a ship objective/task/action/check, a roadmap chunk, or a signal — in the unified Phase-31 SaaS. This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: the Rust core validates against it (serde + a schema test) and the TS edge generates its types from it (json-schema-to-typescript), so the two can never drift. It GENERALIZES the Phase-30a Signal envelope (contract/signal-envelope.schema.json): the cloud fields (schema_version, tenant_id, idempotency_key, source, attribution) are reused verbatim and lifted to the envelope, the local family object is carried verbatim under `record`, and every family's links are normalized into one queryable `edges[]` graph — the product's moat. The signal envelope remains the family=signal profile (see docs/UNIFIED_CONTRACT.md §Relationship to the 30a Signal envelope). See docs/UNIFIED_CONTRACT.md for the prose contract, the per-family idempotency rules, the tenant-identity model, and the edge/graph model.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS envelope schema. Bumped only on a breaking envelope change, independently of any backend, local-record, or signal-envelope version. Integer-as-string form, mirroring docs/SCHEMA.md.

tenant_id.description: The WORKSPACE this record belongs to (wire name kept as tenant_id; 31a-ii). The one hard wall: one workspace = one Durable Object; auth, billing, sync, and isolation bind here; cross-workspace reads are never permitted and the graph never spans workspaces. Two id shapes share the namespace: 'org_…' (a WorkOS organization workspace) and a resolve_project_id() slug (<basename>-<6hex(cwd)> — a single-project workspace from local/email ingest, which merges into an org workspace as a LENS via the aliasing registry). docs/UNIFIED_CONTRACT.md §Workspace identity & isolation.

id.description: The record's stable id, unique within (tenant_id, family, kind). Heterogeneous by family — a think step number ('884'), a ship task/objective/action/check id ('verify-31a', 'action:42'), a roadmap chunk slug ('saas-unified-contract'), or a signal UUIDv4. Pair with `family`+`kind` to address a record; pair with `family` to form an edge endpoint ('<family-prefix>:<id>').

idempotency_key.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 that lets re-delivery / re-sync of the same record collapse to one upsert. Computed per family (docs/UNIFIED_CONTRACT.md §Idempotency): owner-authored records (think/ship/roadmap) use sha256(tenant_id \u241f family \u241f kind \u241f id); ingested signals keep the 30a rule sha256(tenant_id \u241f source.adapter \u241f source.external_id), else sha256(tenant_id \u241f kind \u241f from \u241f body \u241f created). \u241f (U+241F) is the field separator. The canonical store treats a colliding key as a no-op upsert.

created.description: When the record was first created at its origin (RFC 3339 / ISO 8601, UTC).

updated.description: Last mutation time (RFC 3339, UTC). Set by the canonical store on every write; absent on a freshly-created record.

lenses.description: OPTIONAL (31a-ii): the lenses this record is a member of within its workspace — a soft, many-to-many grouping, never a partition. Absent = unlensed (every pre-31a-ii record); for a slug workspace the implicit sole lens is the slug itself, which seeds the records' initial lens on an org merge. idempotency_key NEVER reads this field: the same record in different lenses is the same record. docs/UNIFIED_CONTRACT.md §Lens.

edges.description: The normalized cross-reference graph for this record — the product's moat. Each edge's SOURCE is this record's ('<family-prefix>:<id>') endpoint; `ref` is the TARGET in the existing prefix:value wire form. edges[] is the canonical, queryable projection of however each family stores links locally: roadmap Chunk.cross_refs[] and signal Signal.cross_refs[] map 1:1; a think step's dependencies[] become think:<step> edges (carrying the dependency relation) and its execution_ref becomes one edge; a ship action's think_step becomes a think:<n> edge. Derivable from `record`, but materialized so the backend builds one graph without parsing four local shapes.

record.description: The verbatim local family domain object (a think ThinkStep | ship Objective/Task/Action/Check | roadmap Chunk | Signal). Its detailed shape is owned by the local Rust types (and, for signals, fully specified by contract/signal-envelope.schema.json) and evolves independently, so `additionalProperties` is intentionally OPEN here — the envelope wrapper + edges are the strict contract, the payload is the existing record. The `id` of this record MUST equal the envelope `id`. ONE payload key is contract-owned across every family: `content`, the optional structured body (see $defs/StructuredContent) that lets a record render as UI instead of a prose wall; when present it must be well-formed, and the prose field (`body`/`description`) remains the plain-text fallback for readers that don't know the shape.

Family.description: Which tool family produced the record. The four families that share the think-and-ship server.

Kind.description: The record type within its family. Constrained to the family by the top-level allOf: think\u2192step; ship\u2192objective|task|action|check|gate; roadmap\u2192chunk; signal\u2192signal. A `gate` is an approval gate: agent work paused on a question only a human can answer (docs/UNIFIED_CONTRACT.md \u00a7Approval gates) \u2014 its record carries the question, the option set with a declared safe default, an expiry that resolves an unanswered gate to that default, and \u2014 once decided \u2014 who answered and when.

Edge.description: One directed edge in the cross-ref graph. Source = the enclosing record's ('<family-prefix>:<id>'); target = `ref`. Strict (additionalProperties:false): an edge is a contract object, not a free-form bag.

CrossRef.description: A cross-reference target in the existing wire form `prefix:value`. `prefix` is one of the think/ship/roadmap families, plus `signal`, plus `ext` for an item that lives in an external tracker (`ext:<provider>/<external_id>`). Mirrors infra/cross_ref.rs::CrossRef::from_wire so the same parser accepts it. An `ext:` target has no record of its own in this store, so it appears in the graph as an incoming edge only.

Relation.description: Optional typed relation on an edge. `supports`/`refutes`/`depends_on` mirror the think dependency-edge vocabulary; `realizes` (chunk\u2192task), `motivates` (think\u2192task), and `promoted_from`/`promotes` (signal\u2194chunk) name the cross-family links the graph already expresses. Absent = an unlabeled link.

Source.description: Which edge adapter produced the record and the upstream coordinates needed to dedupe it (Phase 30c). Mainly populated for ingested signals; owner-authored think/ship/roadmap records use source.adapter 'local' or 'mcp', or omit `source` entirely. Reused verbatim from the 30a Signal envelope.

adapter.description: Which edge adapter produced the record. OPEN by design (saga 5b): a closed enum meant registering a new provider required editing this shared contract file and redeploying the Worker before a single event could land. Constrained by SHAPE rather than by value — lowercase snake_case — so a typo is still refused, while a new adapter is a local registration. The values below are the ones that exist today, not the ones permitted.

received_at.description: When the edge accepted the inbound event (RFC 3339, UTC).

StructuredContent.description: The structured body of a record (v1) — a flat, closed set of shapes an agent fills instead of packing everything into prose, so the webapp renders sections, key:value facts, and a one-line summary as real UI. Deliberately NOT a rich-text tree: `summary` is the plain-language headline every card can show, `facts` is the key:value set (status words, counts, ids) that would otherwise be shorthand soup inside a paragraph, and `sections` carry the detail — each a heading plus markdown prose and/or a checklist. Flat by design (a section cannot contain sections) so every renderer is total. Lives at `record.content` for every family; the prose field stays the fallback and legacy records simply omit this.

version.description: Version of the StructuredContent shape itself, independent of the envelope schema_version.

summary.description: One plain-language sentence a card can show whole — what this record says, for a reader with no project context. No internal shorthand, no ids.

facts.description: Short label:value pairs rendered as a fact grid (kind, status, counts, owners). Keep each atomic — a fact is a chip, not a sentence.

sections.description: The detail, one titled section per concern. Order is presentation order.

ContentFact.description: One key:value fact. `label` names the dimension, `value` is the short answer.

ContentSection.description: One titled slice of the record's detail: markdown prose (`prose`), a checklist (`list`), or both. A section never nests.

prose.description: Markdown body for this section (the same subset the prose renderer already speaks: paragraphs, bold/em/code, links, bullet and numbered lists).

list.description: A checklist or plain item list. `done` marks a completed item; omit it for a non-checklist item.

Attribution.description: Structured, optionally-authenticated identity of the author/submitter. `authenticated` is true only when identity was proven via the tenant's OAuth 2.1 auth. Reused verbatim from the 30a Signal envelope.

subject.description: The OAuth 2.1 access-token subject (`sub`) when the author authenticated.
